cards.title: Route-Conditional Feasibility and Assumption Labeling
cards.claim: Feasibility of regimen and formulation parameters is route- and model-conditional. The relevance of fed/fasted state, particle size and other formulation inputs depends on the specific formulation, model structure and intended use. Scenarios should explicitly label assumptions, their basis and uncertainty; unsupported assumptions must not be treated as established facts. Sensitivity analysis should address uncertain parameters relevant to the selected model structure.
conditions: IV simulations: Focus sensitivity on CL, Vss/Vc, and infusion duration; exclude absorption parameters.
Oral simulations: Include GI pH, particle size, and absorption rate in sensitivity analysis if modeled.
All simulations: Must distinguish between measured inputs and assumed/prospective inputs.
required_inputs: Explicit list of assumed parameters (e.g., F, Ka, particle size) with provenance marked as 'assumed' or 'literature-derived'.
Output time grid and dose basis (mg/kg vs. absolute dose).
limitations: A unique multi-compartment curve cannot be derived from CL and Vss alone without additional distribution parameters.
Human variability and clinical validation data are not established for the target drug; simulations are prospective scenarios.
Technical replicates do not increase biological n; group means are not individual trajectories.
cards.downstream_use: Generate a sensitivity analysis plan that perturbs only the parameters relevant to the specific route and model structure. Label all outputs as 'prospective scenario' and flag any parameter lacking experimental or high-quality literature support as an assumption.
cards.retrieval_keywords: Sensitivity analyses and evidence-supported regimen/formulation feasibility

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
